page.layout: One page on the scan, apparently the reverse of a leaf or an endpaper. Upper right: four or five lines of brown-red manuscript ink in a cursive hand, and a few faint lines of show-through below. No printed text block, margin or running head is visible.
page.notes: No printed text is visible on this scan, so nothing is transcribed. The upper lines look like handwriting in brown-red ink, not print, and are excluded under the rules. Lower lines are show-through from the other side. Only a few words in the top lines are even partly legible (for example "in" and "ut" and "cum" in the first lines), and I cannot read them reliably enough to transcribe them. The scan is too faint and the ink too cursive to decide whether the top lines are manuscript annotation or a printed line in an unusual face. If this page is in fact a printed leaf, a higher-resolution or raking-light image of the upper right would let me transcribe it.
